articles.title: Thomas Tuchel says it would be ‘madness’ to rest England players despite longer window
articles.summary: I don’t take calls from Premier League managers, he says. England play Czechia in Prague on Tuesday. Thomas Tuchel says it would be “madness” to allow his England players or the clubs to pick and choose their matches during the elongated Nations League window as he promised to go full throttle for…
body: The manager did accept that Declan Rice needed to rest and could not be part of the squad in light of the Arsenal midfielder’s heavy workload across a number of seasons and well-documented fitness issues. Rice was at Wembley on Saturday to watch England lose 3-2 against Spain in their opening Nations League game.

But now that Tuchel has his group, he says there is no room for compromise and certainly not to speak to club managers who might want to make deals over their players’ minutes. Tuchel does not want to rotate his starting personnel, although he does accept it could be impractical. After Prague, England go to Rijeka to play Croatia on Saturday before returning to Wembley to face Czechia next Tuesday.

“I don’t take calls from Premier League managers,” Tuchel said. “I never called any national team coach [when he was in club football]. I cannot manage [the minutes of] the players. It’s just impossible. I knew as a club coach … if I would call a coach in Brazil or Argentina, they would not know what I am talking about. The players would not know what I am talking about.

articles.title: James Trafford’s England dream burns with No 1 spot finally up for grabs again
articles.summary: The Leeds player was surprise starter against Spain but, after his solid display, Jordan Pickford’s grip may be loosening. James Trafford looks genuinely affronted. The Leeds goalkeeper’s reaction borders on incredulity.
body: Defiance is the stock in trade of a goalkeeper and Trafford has a nice line in it, on and off the pitch. Thrust into the England lineup against Spain at Wembley on Saturday for only his third cap, he performed well, particularly during the opening 35 minutes when the world champions threatened to run riot. Trafford made two excellent saves that kept England in contention, laying the groundwork for their surge into a 2-1 half-time lead. They ended up losing 3-2 in the Nations League opener after Harry Kane missed a 54th-minute penalty for 3-1.

The question to Trafford was valid because everybody remembers the situation. How he rejoined City, the club of his youth, from Burnley in July last year, ready to be Pep Guardiola’s No 1; the replacement for Ederson, who departed after eight seasons of stellar service. And how, after three Premier League matches, Guardiola went out and signed Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain, installing him as his first-choice goalkeeper.

articles.title: Bellamy 'hurting' after Denmark outclass Wales
articles.summary: Craig Bellamy says he is "hurting" on the back of Wales' 2-0 Nations League A defeat away to Denmark, but feels his side will continue to improve.
body: Craig Bellamy says he is "hurting" after admitting Denmark were worthy winners against his Wales side in Copenhagen.
A Ben Davies own goal along with Gustav Isaksen's strike earned Brian Riemer's men a 2-0 victory over Wales at Parken Stadium.
It leaves Bellamy's team without a win in six matches in 2026 and without a point from their away Nations League A double-header with Portugal and the Danes.
Despite the loss, Bellamy remains confident his side will improve by playing against Europe's elite on a consistent basis.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev clinches Laver Cup for Team Europe with victory over Learner Tien
articles.summary: Jakub Mensik and Flavio Cobolli win doubles 7-5, 6-3. Andre Agassi goads Alexander Zverev at ceremony. Team Europe reclaimed their Laver Cup title with a dominant 13-5 victory against Team World on the final day of competition at the O2 Arena.
body: The contest had been finely poised after two days’ play, with Team Europe holding a narrow 7-5 lead at the beginning of the day. With each match worth three points on Sunday, Europe needed two victories out of the four remaining matches to win. They clinched their victory efficiently.

Jakub Mensik and Flavio Cobolli opened the day with a 7-5, 6-3 win against Alex de Minaur and Taylor Fritz before Alexander Zverev, the recent French and US Open champion, closed out the series with a 7-6 (3), 6-3 win against Learner Tien.

This was a logical result. The No 2, Alexander Zverev, the No 3, Carlos Alcaraz, and the No 7, Flavio Cobolli, are all ranked more highly than Team World’s highest-ranked players, Alex de Minaur and Fritz, and there is just much more depth in a continent that has won the past 67 men’s grand slam titles. The last non-European player to win a men’s grand slam title was Argentina’s Juan Martín del Potro at the 2009 US Open.

articles.title: Heroic York rearguard stuns Wigan in Grand Final
articles.summary: York Valkyrie become the first side to win the Women's Super League three times after an incredible defensive effort thwarts favourites Wigan.
body: York Valkyrie became the first side to win the Women's Super League three times after an incredible defensive effort thwarted Wigan Warriors at the Brick Community Stadium.
Under siege for much of a scoreless second half, York stood firm to claim a surprise win over the favourites.
Teenager Amelie Lenham, the player of the match, led the way with a series of crucial interventions as a first-half try from Sinead Peach, plus two goals from Ellie Williamson, proved just enough.
Wigan - who had their only try-scorer Mia-Jayne Atherton and Eva Hunter sin-binned in the first half - were left stunned after an uncharacteristically error-strewn display.

articles.title: Fernandes, Gakpo & Dorgu join injury list
articles.summary: Bruno Fernandes, Cody Gakpo and Patrick Dorgu all join the international break's high-profile injury list after suffering issues that have curtailed their involvement in Nations League matches.
body: After playing in Portugal's win over Wales on Thursday, Manchester United captain Fernandes was not in the squad for Sunday's fixture against Norway.
Prior to the match boss Jorge Jesus revealed, external Fernandes had "played through the pain" against Wales and "wasn't his usual self".
"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," he said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."
Meanwhile, both Fernandes' United team-mate Dorgu and Liverpool striker Gakpo suffered injuries during games for their respective countries on Sunday.

articles.title: Willson Contreras back in Red Sox lineup for regular season finale
articles.summary: Three days after casting doubt on his availability for the postseason, Red Sox slugger Willson Contreras is back in the lineup for Boston’s regular season finale Sunday — and there’s hope he might be available Tuesday when the playoffs begin.
body: Contreras is hitting third and serving as Boston’s designated hitter against the Cubs and lefty Shota Imanaga in a neutral site game between the clubs at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. Major League Baseball moved the game to Florida due to a significant rainstorm in New England this weekend.

Contreras has not played in a game in 10 days — since Sept. 17 — when he was hit in the hand by a pitch during the eighth inning of a Red Sox win over the Rangers. He has avoided the injured list but before Saturday, struggled to progress to a point where he could swing a bat comfortably on back-to-back days. As of Friday, Contreras’ outlook for his postseason availability seemed bleak. Clearly, the last 48 hours have included improvement for Contreras, who will try to get through Sunday’s game without pain ahead of Game 1 of the Wild Card Series on Tuesday in New York.
According to manager Chad Tracy, Contreras’ hand showed marked improvement during a team workout at Tropicana Field on Saturday.

articles.title: No handshakes between Republic of Ireland and Israel
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland and Israel players do not shake hands with each other before Sunday's controversial Uefa Nations League game in Hungary.
body: After walking on to the pitch at Nagyerdei Stadion, the Republic of Ireland squad stood for their national anthem and appeared to bow their heads before Israel's anthem.
Following the anthems, the two teams did not line up for the traditional handshakes.
There was also no exchange of pennants between Republic of Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel skipper Manor Solomon, who did not shake hands.
The fixtures have been embroiled in controversy since February when the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

articles.title: Gabe Vincent Is Betting On Himself Over Knicks Camp Deal
articles.summary: Gabe Vincent is playing a high-stakes game with his career right now. The veteran guard, who recently played 24 regular season games for the Atlanta Hawks, is still looking for a home. It is wild to see a player of his caliber sitting on the market this late in the summer.
body: The New York Knicks were looking at Vincent for a spot on their camp roster. They have already signed five veterans to deals for training camp. However, Vincent chose not to take that path. The Stein Line’s Jake Fischer reported that the ex-Hawk preferred to “wait for a more sure-fire opportunity,” per Soaring Down South.

I think he is making the right call. He is a proven vet. He shouldn’t have to go through a camp trial just to prove he belongs on a roster. Taking a camp deal with the Knicks would have been a lot of work for a lot of little reward. He knows his value. Teams still need a steady hand to handle the ball, and he can provide that.

Vincent provided some real stability for the Hawks’ second unit late last season. While his stats were not massive, the young Hawks roster was desperate for another person who could run the offense. He is an underrated piece of the puzzle. If he lands a guaranteed deal before the season starts, this move to wait will look very smart.

articles.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
articles.summary: Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.
body: India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.
In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."
Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

articles.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa
articles.summary: Australia fell to an ODI series defeat to South Africa with a game to spare as they were beaten by 32 runs in the second ODI match of three in Johannesburg on Sunday.
body: David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.
Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

articles.title: Imperious Banton century propels England to Sri Lanka series victory
articles.summary: Tom Banton posted an imperious 126 off just 105 balls to guide England to a dominant 223-run win in the third ODI against Sri Lanka to secure a 2-1 series victory at the Oval.
body: Banton top scored with his career-best but was aided by sizeable contributions by skipper Harry Brook (77 off 66) and the in-form Jordan Cox (76 off 52) as the batting side set the tourists a mammoth target of 356 after their 50 overs, with Dilhara Fernando (3-52) the pick of the bowlers - albeit with two of his wickets coming with the final two balls of the innings.
That target loomed even larger over Sri Lanka's innings when Sonny Baker nicked off Pathum Nissanka (1) for his maiden ODI wicket with just the eighth ball of their innings.

From there the wickets started to tumble for Sri Lanka who - despite the best efforts of captain Kusal Mendis (35 off 26) - went from 36-1 to 82-6 in just 10 overs, including the confusing run-out dismissal of Pavan Rathnayake (18), which was still given as out despite Jordan Cox taking the bails off before Archer's direct-hit throw dismantled the stumps.

The impressive bowling of Liam Dawson (3-17) and Gus Atkinson (2-26) then ensured Sri Lanka's tail went out with a 50-run whimper, handing England the series victory and marking a successful end of the home summer for Brendon McCullum's side after 12 wins in 14 white-ball games.
